name: aios
//files: Allowlist, not a convenience: agents/ is the USER's org (and on this machine carries a client's agent + prompt), so it must never ship — the runtime creates it and seeds it from templates/. templates/_capabilities.yaml is product data seedCapabilities() throws without, so templates/ MUST ship. dist/src/ not dist/: tsconfig compiles test/ too, so dist/test/ holds client-named fixtures. NOTE: `files` OVERRIDES .gitignore, which is why gitignored dist/ ships at all.

scripts.//build: Clean first: tsc never prunes outputs whose source was deleted or renamed, so dist/ accumulated modules that no longer exist in src/ (packs/, finance/agent, engine/executor, engine/jobs) and npm pack shipped them as dead code. A renamed guard kept its old client-named file alive there too.
